stem: The following statements describe the term of “chimerism” after allogeneic HSCT. Select the CORRECT answer.

options.A: Although rare, some cases of hematological malignancies may have long-term survival despite persistent presence of mixed chimerism.
options.B: Mixed chimerism indicates the human body has 100% hematopoietic cells of donor origin within bone marrow, mixed with cells of recipient origin at other organs.
options.C: For patients of severe aplastic anemia receiving allogeneic HSCT, persistence of mixed chimerism usually indicates inevitable graft failure in the near future.
options.D: Chimerism can be readily determined using short tandem repeat (STR) test based on PCR method for a single locus of genomic DNA sequence.

ebmt_chapters: Ch21 Documentation of Engraftment and Chimerism After HCT (PDF p210–215)
Ch78 Acquired Bone Marrow Failure: Severe Aplastic Anemia and Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PDF p695–703)

stem: Which of the following cases is least likely to be cured after allogeneic HSCT ?

options.A: Primary induction failure after 2 cycles of standard 7+3 inductions.
options.D: Relapsed AML refractory to salvage chemotherapy

stem: Select CORRECT answer from the following statements about minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment in adult ALL.

options.A: The commonly used techniques of MRD assessment include short-tandem repeat (STR) analysis, fusion gene transcript detection, NGS, and flow cytometry.
options.B: For a young adult ALL of standard risk with significant reduction of MRD after induction and undetectable MRD after consolidation, subsequent transplantation would provide further survival benefit.
options.C: When MRD assessment is not available, transplantation for a young adult in CR1 with suitable donor may provide survival benefit.
options.D: For an adult ALL harboring t(9;22) with MRD being undetectable by RQ-PCR after consolidation, transplantation is generally not indicated.

ebmt_chapters: Ch72 Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia in Adults (PDF p642–650)
Ch57 Monitoring Measurable Residual Disease in ALL and AML (PDF p516–524)

stem: About transplantation in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), which statement is wrong?

options.A: Donor lymphocyte infusion is an option when molecular relapse detected after transplantation
options.B: Patients with persistent positive BCR-ABL 2 months post-transplantation carried higher relapse risk than those with BCR-ABL turning detectable 8 month post-transplantation
options.C: For elderly patients, reduced intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen offers less toxicity but still has the graft-versus leukemia effect
options.D: Although lack of definite evidence, maintaining tyrosin kinase inhibitor (TKI) use after transplantation is suggested in those who transplanted in accelerated phase

stem: High-dose chemotherapy with BEAM followed by autologous HSCT is the standard of care for patients with chemo-sensitive relapse diffuse large B cell lymphoma. Which of the following statements is wrong?

options.A: Randomized studies confirmed significant differences in terms of efficacy or toxicity with different salvage regimens prior to autologous HSCT
options.B: The objective of salvage chemotherapy is to induce a complete or partial response indicating that the tumor remains chemosensitive, this having a major impact on outcome after transplantation
options.C: PET negativity after salvage therapy is a surrogate marker of chemosensitivity and predicts patient outcome after autologous HSCT
options.D: Allogeneic HSCT should be considered in younger patients without comorbidities especially in patients with refractory disease or early relapse

stem: Which is the most important adverse prognostic factor that impacts long-term outcome of diffuse large B cell lymphoma patients being treated with allogeneic HSCT?

options.A: Early relapse within 12 months of induction therapy
options.C: Involvement of two or more extranodal sites at relapse

stem: Which of the following statement is wrong?

stem: Which of the following statements in regarding to myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is INCORRECT?

options.A: Allogeneic HSCT remains the treatment of choice for patients with advanced stage MDS.
options.B: Reduced-Intensity conditioning (RIC) regimens have extended the use of allogeneic HSCT to patients up to the age of 70 years.
options.C: MDS patients who received bone marrow stem cells had a faster engraftment and a lower relapse rate compare to blood stem cells.
options.D: MDS patients with intermediate 2 and higher risk will have best survival if transplantation is performed early after diagnosis.
